## bijection_verdict
**PASS.** No atom dropped, softened or added; retired surface carried as retired with correct scope; all factor ladders complete. Notes (not KB defects):
- N1 (framework, out of KB scope): GT step `verify_customer_identity` rests on the runtime system background; no tires-policy atom; not judged here.
- N2 (cross-product naming, informational): the line figure `original_tread_depth_32nds` is published under its schema label "New-tire tread depth" (line card, storage surcharge, truck-size restock docs). The hazard corpus reads it as "the tire line's original tread depth … from the Tire Sets & Treadwear Limited Warranty line"; the phrase "original tread depth" never occurs in docs/tires and `KB_search("original tread depth Tire Sets line")` does not surface the line card in the top 3. Findable by synonym; does not touch a tires score. The other requested per-line figures are published under their official names: "Mount and balance, per tire", "Scrap tire handling fee", "Warranted miles", "Set instant savings, per ticket" with "Tires of the line needed on one ticket", "Complimentary alignment check at installation", tender table in `refund_tender_rules`; tire-set status meanings are carried per transition (installation -> active, cancellation -> cancelled, trial return -> returned, closure -> worn out / retired).
- N3 (source-side, base): `lifecycle` worn_out "means" says "adjusted … or replaced", while the base closure rule (carried verbatim) says worn out once every position "carries an adjustment". Authoring metadata only; does not move a scored value.
- N4 (source-side visibility): no rule or document says which record carries "the store's selling price of the same tire on the adjustment date"; GT uses the ordered replacement ticket T-15093342 written 2026-10-08 (six days before the adjustment date). Only one candidate exists on the visible surface, so the scored value is unique; it moves no value here but is an undefined data source in the base clause.
- N5 (source-side, rule vs compute): the road hazard line's "plan's price for one tire" is unrounded in the compute, while the hazard price schedule rounds the percentage price half up before the min/max. Does not move 109.59 (half line 13.59915 unrounded vs 13.60 from a rounded 27.20: balances 109.58915 and 109.59000 both round to 109.59).
- N6 (base order sentence, policy-side): `open_tire_limit_per_vehicle` "that older set is retired first and only then is the new ticket opened" is base law carried as written.
